entities.summary: Manius Tullius Longus, a Roman consul in 500 BC, played a pivotal role in shaping the course of Roman history. He was a key figure in the political landscape of ancient Rome, serving as consul alongside Servius Sulpicius Camerinus Cornutus. This partnership marked a significant shift in the balance of power at Rome, as the two men worked to strengthen the Roman Republic and assert its dominance over the Mediterranean. Their collaborative efforts had a lasting impact on the development of Roman law, governance, and politics, which in turn influenced the trajectory of Western civilization. Manius Tullius Longus is remembered as a visionary leader who helped to lay the foundations for Rome's future success. The Roman historian Livy credited Longus with the creation of the 'Auctor Vitae Romanorum,' a seminal work on Roman history that would go on to shape the narrative of the Roman Republic for centuries to come.
